blocks.passage:
Most feedback at work is either too vague to be useful or too harsh to be heard. Vague feedback — "you did a great job" — feels nice but does not help anyone grow. Harsh feedback — "that was terrible" — closes the conversation before it even starts.

Useful feedback is specific and behavioural. Instead of "you were unclear in the meeting", try "when you moved from the budget numbers to the forecast, I lost the connection — can you tell me how you saw the link?" That is something you can actually respond to.

Receiving feedback is also a skill. Good professionals learn to resist their first reaction — usually defensive — and stay curious for a few seconds longer. Ask for the example behind the comment. Say thank you, even when it stings. Decide later what to do with it.

items.q: What are the two ways feedback commonly fails, according to the text?
options: Too vague to be useful, or too harsh to be heard
items.why: "either too vague to be useful or too harsh to be heard."

items.q: What makes feedback useful, according to the text?
items.why: "Useful feedback is specific and behavioural."

items.q: Why is "when you moved from the budget to the forecast, I lost the connection" better than "you were unclear"?
options: It points to a specific behaviour the person can respond to
items.why: "That is something you can actually respond to."

items.q: What does the text say is usually our first reaction to feedback?
items.why: "resist their first reaction — usually defensive."

items.q: "Say thank you, even when it stings" suggests that receiving feedback well means…
options: staying open even when the comment is uncomfortable
items.why: Inferência: agradecer mesmo quando incomoda é manter-se aberto e decidir depois o que fazer.

audio.text:
Thanks for making time. I wanted to talk about the client meeting yesterday — and I want to be specific, not vague, because you're good and I think this is worth getting right.

Here's what I noticed. When the client pushed back on the numbers, you answered three questions at once, quite fast. I could see the client stop taking notes at that point. My read is that the pace lost them, not the content — the content was solid.

So this isn't a 'you did badly' conversation. It's one specific thing: when the pressure went up, the pace went up too. Next time, what if you slowed down and took the questions one at a time?

How did it feel from your side? I'd genuinely like to hear how you saw that moment — you were in the room and I was only watching.

And to be clear, the relationship is fine. The client emailed this morning; they want to continue. This is about making a strong performance even stronger.

items.q: How does Sophie frame the feedback at the start?
options: As specific, not vague, and worth getting right
items.why: "I want to be specific, not vague, because you're good and I think this is worth getting right."

items.q: What specific behaviour did Sophie notice?
options: Under pressure, the pace sped up and the client stopped taking notes
items.why: "when the pressure went up, the pace went up too" — o cliente parou de anotar.

items.q: What was NOT the problem, according to Sophie?
items.why: "the pace lost them, not the content — the content was solid."

items.q: What does Sophie ask the analyst?
options: How the moment felt from their side
items.why: "How did it feel from your side? I'd genuinely like to hear how you saw that moment."

items.q: Why does Sophie mention the client's email?
options: To reassure them that the relationship is fine
items.why: "the relationship is fine. The client emailed this morning; they want to continue."

items.q: "Try to be **specific** rather than general." Specific means…
items.why: Specific = específico, preciso.

items.q: "Give **behavioural** feedback." Behavioural feedback focuses on…
items.why: Behavioural = comportamental, sobre a ação concreta.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "He got **defensive** and ___ the comment instead of listening."
items.why: Defensive = defensivo; a reação é rejeitar em vez de ouvir.

items.q: A **blind spot** is…
options: something about yourself you cannot easily see
items.why: Blind spot = ponto cego, o que você não enxerga em si.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "Good feedback is ___ — it helps the person improve."
items.why: Constructive = construtivo.

items.q: "Can I give you some feedback? Feel free to **push back** if you disagree." To push back means to…
items.why: Push back = contestar respeitosamente.

items.q: "I know this is hard to hear, but **bear with me**." To bear with someone means to…
items.why: Bear with me = tenha paciência comigo.

items.q: "Let's not **sugar-coat** it — the deadline was missed." To sugar-coat means to…
options: make something sound nicer than it is
items.why: Sugar-coat = suavizar demais, dourar a pílula.

items.q: "Take it **on board** and see what fits." To take something on board means to…
items.why: Take on board = levar em conta, absorver.

items.q: "I'll **own** my part in what went wrong." To own something means to…
items.why: To own = assumir a responsabilidade.
